diagnosis_explanation:
Your urine had blood in it. This problem is now gone.

You also have a prostate problem. It is not cancer. Doctors also found a cyst on your kidney. It is not growing. We are watching it.

You have some joint pain. This is from a problem called osteoarthritis.
medication_rationale:
Colace 100 mg twice daily:
This medicine helps soften your stool. This makes it easier to pass. It is for your comfort. You may notice your bowel movements are softer. This is normal. There are no common side effects to worry about. Call your doctor if you have a severe stomach ache.

Ciprofloxacin:
This medicine is an antibiotic. It helps fight infections. You are taking it for a short time. You may get an upset stomach or diarrhea. These are usually mild. Call your doctor if you get a rash or hives. Also call if you have severe stomach pain.

Lasix:
This medicine helps your body remove extra fluid. This can make you urinate more often. It can help lower blood pressure. You may feel dizzy sometimes. This is normal. Call your doctor if you get muscle cramps. Also call if you feel very weak. Call 911 right away if you have sudden face drooping, arm weakness, or trouble speaking.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired after your procedure.
- You can do your normal daily activities.
- Do not worry if you see some pink in your urine.
- Call your doctor if you see bright red blood in your urine.
- Call your doctor if you stop making urine.
- Your goal this week is to rest and heal.

**Week 2:**
- You may feel a little stronger this week.
- Continue with your normal daily activities.
- Call your doctor if you see bright red blood in your urine.
- Call your doctor if you stop making urine.
- Your goal this week is to increase your walking a little.

**Week 3:**
- You should feel more energy this week.
- You can return to your normal diet.
- Keep doing your normal daily activities.
- Call your doctor if you see bright red blood in your urine.
- Call your doctor if you stop making urine.
- Your goal this week is to return to your normal routine.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel back to your usual self.
- Continue with all your normal activities.
- Call your doctor if you see bright red blood in your urine.
- Call your doctor if you stop making urine.
- Your goal this week is to stay active and eat well.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You should feel much better by now.
- Keep up with your normal activities.
- Contact your doctor if symptoms return.
- Healing takes time, so be patient with yourself.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Worsening blood in urine: This can mean bad bleeding.
- No urine output: Your kidneys may be failing now.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Complex cyst or tumor: This needs more study today.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Questions about your medicine: Your doctor can help you plan.
